According to a fairly reliable tipster, next year could see the launch of the largest-screened iPhone ever.

Supply chain sources say Apple is testing a new display panel that could be used in a new iPhone whose model name remains unknown…

The Mystery Of Next Year's Flagship iPhone Naming

2027 will mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, and for years there has been persistent speculation that Apple is preparing a special product to mark the occasion. This year, Apple is expected to come very close to realising its long-held iPhone design vision — a 'single slab of glass.'

Some believe Apple could launch a standalone 20th anniversary edition iPhone, similar to the iPhone X of its day. However, more recent reports indicate that this groundbreaking new device will be released directly as next year's Pro models — the iPhone 19 Pro and Pro Max.

A third possibility is that Apple could leap straight from the iPhone 18 to the iPhone 20 to mark the milestone.

The Largest iPhone Screen Ever

Leaker "Digital Chat Station" (DCS) says supply chain information indicates Apple is testing its largest-ever iPhone screen. However, the size increase is quite modest compared to the existing 6.9-inch iPhone 17 Pro Max.

In other words, they believe Apple will market it as a 7-inch screen.

DCS does not have information on what this new screen would be used for — assuming Apple ultimately follows through — but he speculates that regardless of the final brand name, this screen could be used in next year's iPhone Pro Max.

9to5Mac's Take

Apple tests all sorts of things, and most of them never actually reach the market, so even if this screen prototype does exist in the supply chain, that doesn't necessarily mean it will end up in an iPhone.

That said, if Apple's goal is to achieve a 'single slab of glass' effect, then marketing the largest-ever screen does seem entirely logical.
